Wren seen as a factory: each stage of a pipeline produces at some rate and consumes at another, and the slowest stage, or a queue that holds what a stage made, sets the throughput. This page has the map with numbers, the bottleneck of each pipeline, an inventory of what goes against the rules below, and what to do next, ranked.

The rules the work follows: data laid out for the loops that read it (struct of arrays where a loop reads a few fields of many items, flat arrays rather than hash tables, indices rather than pointers); no cache to hide a slow path (the caches that are a product, the HTTP cache, the back/forward cache, compiled code on disk, stay); lists with an inline capacity rather than heap lists; bitsets rather than arrays of bools; no mutex where an ownership hand-off, per-thread state, an SPSC ring or an MPSC queue does; explicit state machines in structures.

#How it was measured

On the development machine (2026-11-02), headless (api.Window_Mode.Headless: no window, nothing takes the focus), the profile build (build.bat profile, -define:PROFILE=true) with the native library of the development builds (Cargo quick: text shaping 2 to 5 % slower than the shipped one, see native/Cargo.toml). Tools:

  • wrentool bench perf -Only <scenario>: start to load, frames, CPU, memory, and the browser's own report per scenario (build/perf/<scenario>.txt: per-phase statistics of the frames, the start-up marks, the style and layout passes; .csv: one row per frame).
  • A load measured from the navigation (not from the process start): the page is opened on about:blank, then api.navigate, then the Navigation Timing entry read with api.eval (responseEnd - fetchStart, domInteractive - responseEnd), then the scenario's input, then api.stats (CPU, frames, the loop's meter: loop.turns, sleeps, causes).
  • WREN_SAMPLE=1 (1 ms samples of the window's thread, by phase), WREN_SAMPLE_STACK=1 (callers), WREN_SAMPLE_THREADS=1 (the other threads: those the system's list says are on a processor or waiting for one, each followed every millisecond until it goes back into the system; per thread, its name, hottest call chains and the functions on its stack). The list takes 30 ms on a machine with many processes, so a burst of a few ms is caught by chance: 145 samples, 123 running, on 15 s of p10k_renav. Before round 3 it visited the ninety threads in turn, about 13 samples a second each; from round 3 to 24 it took the one whose cycles moved most; rounds 25 to 27 every thread that ran in the last second (0 of 44 807 samples running on p10k_renav). Stacks are walked in a copy, after the thread has gone on (crashtrace.Stack_Copy). Samples that land in a system call are biased: on the script-heavy page NtUserGetQueueStatus (the chrome's preemption checking for input) took 13 % of the samples, and turning preemption off (browser.shell.preempt=false) changed neither the frame rate nor the CPU.

Numbers are medians of 5 runs unless a range is given; the machine runs other programs, so CPU per second moves by a factor of 2 from run to run, frame times much less.

#Profilers

Beside the built-in profiler, Wren speaks to four external ones. What they see of Wren comes from one place, package trace (src/trace): the phases of a frame (Phase, src/browser/prof.odin) are its zones, named as above, on the window's thread; a frame mark at each present; the start-up's marks (the profile build). Without its switches every call of it is empty and nothing is linked: build\wren.exe imports none of ETW's writing functions and holds no Tracy client (test_all checks it). The zones of a thread pair on every path: an end closes what an early return left open, and each frame begins by closing whatever the last one left.

Threads have names (SetThreadDescription, which Tracy, WPA, VTune and the debuggers read): wren-window, wren-page-layout, wren-style and wren-layout (the style and layout pools; the compositor's work runs on the latter), wren-js-compile, wren-js-worker, wren-wasm-compile, wren-wasm-epoch, wren-wasm-cache, wren-image-decode, wren-blocking-<n>, the media's.

Symbols: every variant but the release has its PDB beside it (build\wren_prof.pdb...). For WPA and VTune, the system's from Microsoft's server:

set _NT_SYMBOL_PATH=S:\wren\build;srv*C:\symbols*https://msdl.microsoft.com/download/symbols

#Instructions`n

jsengine cost --pref wasm.wasmtime.fuel=true examples\jsbench\cost.js: what each case of the file costs in Wasm instructions an iteration, interpreted, deterministic (wasm.wasmtime.fuel; local.get counts: compare a path with itself). For a change of the engine on a busy machine, before any wall clock.

#Tracy

Tracy 0.14.1, pinned by SHA-256 (src/tools/wrentool/deps/tracy.odin): its client built from the source release into build\tracy\tracy.lib by the builds that ask for it, its viewer from the release's Windows build. The client records only while a viewer is connected (TRACY_ON_DEMAND) and answers on this machine only (TRACY_ONLY_LOCALHOST, port 8086).

set WREN_TRACY=1
build.bat profile                         (-> build\wren_prof_tracy.exe; any variant: build\wren_tracy.exe...)
build\wrentool fetch tracy                (-> build\tracy\tracy-profiler.exe, tracy-capture.exe)
build\wren_prof_tracy.exe examples\jsbench\nodes10k.html
build\tracy\tracy-profiler.exe            the client is listed: Connect
build\tracy\tracy-capture.exe -a 127.0.0.1 -o build\perf\nodes10k.tracy -s 10    (no window: 10 s into a file the viewer opens)
build\tracy\tracy-csvexport.exe build\perf\nodes10k.tracy                    (each zone's count, mean and total, as CSV)

It shows the phases, the frames, a plot of the layout items per frame, and in a Tracy build every call of a module into the browser (each import of the JavaScript engine: a DOM call, a style or layout read) as a zone module.name on the thread that made it (src/wasm/host_trace.odin). Run elevated, Tracy also samples the CPU and shows context switches (its own ETW session). Not there: GPU zones (the toolkit keeps its Direct3D 11 device and context to itself, its timestamp queries are the renderer's: gpu_steps.odin reads their results), lock annotations (Odin's sync.Mutex has no hook). Connected, it costs: 5 s of nodes10k made 6.5 million zones (2.2 million dom.Node_preInsert alone), and 44 frames a second instead of 230; the phases alone are a few hundred zones a second.

#VTune (and perf)

Wasmtime tells a profiler about the code it compiles when wasm.wasmtime.profiler says which (a restart preference; none by default): vtune (Windows and Linux on x86-64: the prebuilt library has Intel's ITT API), perfmap and jitdump (Linux's perf). The code read from the compiled-code cache is told too. The JavaScript engine's image keeps its functions' names (its name section: wasm-ld --strip-debug drops only DWARF, which buildjs -names keeps):

vtune -collect hotspots -result-dir build\vtune\nodes10k -- build\wren_prof.exe --pref wasm.wasmtime.profiler=vtune examples\jsbench\nodes10k.html
vtune -report hotspots -result-dir build\vtune\nodes10k -format csv

(jspage --pref wasm.wasmtime.profiler=vtune is the engine alone.) VTune then lists the engine's functions as [Dynamic code], wasmtime::jsrt::interp_run, wasmtime::jscapi::...::bridge_invoke, wasmtime::jsrt::call_native; telling it about every function costs about 1.2 s of CPU at the start (Wasmtime's VTuneAgent::register_function).

#WPR and WPA

The profile build (-define:WREN_ETW=true in any other) is an ETW provider, Wren.Browser, a TraceLogging one (each event describes itself: no manifest to install), GUID 10e6f595-25dd-53c9-a97c-bdec823560e6 (TraceLogging's hash of the name). Each zone is a Start and a Stop event named after its phase; Presented at each present; Mark with the start-up's steps. While no session listens an event costs the test of a flag. tools\wren.wprp records CPU samples with stacks, context switches with the thread that readied each, the GPU's scheduler (DxgKrnl) and the provider; tools\wren_regions.xml makes the phases WPA's regions of interest.

build\wrentool trace start                (an elevated prompt: WPR asks for one, wrentool does not)
build\wren_prof.exe examples\jsbench\nodes10k.html
build\wrentool trace stop                 (-> build\trace\wren.etl)
wpa build\trace\wren.etl                  Trace > Load Symbols; Trace > Trace Properties > Regions of Interest: tools\wren_regions.xml

Checked on 2026-11-04 (WPR and WPA of the Windows Performance Toolkit 11.8): 3 s of nodes10k give 1 082 regions of each phase that runs every frame, the start-up's marks, Wren's functions named from the PDB, DxgKrnl's events. xperf -i build\trace\wren.etl -a regions -man tools\wren_regions.xml lists the regions without a window.

The profile build with ETW in it and no session, against the one before it (5 interleaved runs of nodes10k, 5 s, median): CPU work per frame p50 17.70 -> 17.54 ms, Animation p50 11.79 -> 11.66 ms, 222.0 -> 227.7 frames/s: no cost seen.

#PIX

PIX's GPU captures are of Direct3D 12 programs: Wren's Direct3D 11 renderer is not one, the wgpu backend (WREN_RENDER=wgpu, Direct3D 12 on Windows) is. Its timing captures read their own markers (WinPixEventRuntime), not another provider: nothing of Wren's is added for it; WPA shows the same phases.

#The map

Times are per load or per frame on the window's thread unless said; "items/s" is what the stage gets through.

#1. A large static page, loaded (build/perf/p10k.html: 611 KB, 10 020 elements, 16 478 layout items, 2 000 rules)

stagewheretimeratewaits on
network bytes (file://)loader thread2 to 5 ms~200 MB/sthe disk
decode, parse, DOMblocking pool (page/offthread.odin)26 to 31 ms~20 MB/s, ~350 000 elements/sthe body
hand-over to the loopposted task (host.post)was 620 to 1000 ms, now 0the loop's next turn
adopt, revealwindow thread< 3 ms
style, full passwindow thread + style pool (7 threads)17 to 29 ms (+ 6 to 11 ms engine rebuild)0.6 to 1 M elements/s
layout, first full passlayout thread13 to 30 ms (31 to 63 ms forced by a script read, style included)~0.5 to 1 M items/sstyle
paint (display items)window thread6 to 11 ms the first frame, then 0.02 mslayout
GPU drawGPU0.09 ms
present0.08 to 0.4 msthe swap chain

navigate -> load event: 1055 ms -> 34 ms; domInteractive - responseEnd: 1035 ms -> 32 ms; until the page is quiet: 1516 ms -> 480 ms (5 runs each, build\wren_prof before and after the change below).

Bottleneck (fixed): the hand-over. The parsed document waited in the loop's queue for 0.6 to 1 s while the window's thread slept in its frame pacer: headless frames made at once for a waiting client each booked a frame slot ahead of the clock, and the first paced frame after the burst paid them all back. Now: parse plus the first style and layout pass, about 60 to 90 ms, the parse off the window's thread.

Not measured further: from the process's creation to main took 1.0 to 4.4 s in these runs (the start-up marks of the report), before any code of ours: the loader and the antivirus on a freshly linked 59 MB executable.

#2. A script-heavy page (examples/jsbench/nodes10k.html: 10 000 nodes made and removed per frame)

stagetime per frameshare of the window thread's samplesnotes
script: JS engine and DOM calls29 ms p50 (1.3 to 3 s at p99)50 %~20 000 DOM calls a frame (create, append, remove): ~1 µs each with the engine around them

paint, chrome3.6 + 3.6 ms7 %

31 to 35 frames/s at 60 Hz, 7.7 at 180 Hz; 1.2 to 1.7 cores; 1.1 to 1.35 GB private memory. The style engine holds 580 019 styled elements for 12 510 layout items: removed nodes live until the garbage collector frees their wrappers, so handle indices grow and every array indexed by them with them, and partial restyles leave so much behind that 40 of the 43 full passes are "memory left by partial restyles".

After round 2 (medians of 5 runs of each build, interleaved, js_nodes10k at 180 Hz, 8 s):

beforeafter
frames/s28.342.9
CPU work per frame, mean103 ms67 ms
script (Animation phase)54 ms42 ms
style14.1 ms9.8 ms
layout (waits on the layout thread)27.8 ms10.9 ms
styled elements (entries of by_node)840 00010 000 to 20 000
private memory1.27 GB305 MB

Every style pass is now a full one ("too much changed": 10 000 changed of 20 000 live nodes) at 9.6 ms; before, 160 partial restyles of 13 to 16 ms and 43 full passes of 12 to 15 ms. The collections the DOM now asks for (below) are about a quarter of the window thread's samples: the cost of freeing the wrappers moved there from the engine's own collections.

After round 3 (medians of 5 runs of each build, interleaved): styles made by a full pass 20.1 -> 11.1 MB, the pass 9.4 -> 8.8 ms, private memory 302 -> 275 MB, CPU work per frame 63.0 -> 61.7 ms. On the page thread, where layout runs, the samples in NtFreeVirtualMemory (its temporary memory given back after every pass) went from 2.7 to 3.2 % to none. The style stage is a restyle of the 7 500 new elements whichever way it goes: with partial restyles allowed (style.incremental.max_ratio=1) each costs 8.9 ms against 8.3 ms for a full pass, and the style stage per frame is the same (8.1 against 8.3 ms).

Where the script stage goes (round 3, before its change; WREN_SAMPLE_STACK=1 WREN_SAMPLE_UNDER=page::run_animation_frames for the browser's side, jspage -image <engine built with buildjs -names> -profile for the engine's, and micro-benchmarks of single calls in jspage). A frame makes about 65 000 crossings from Wasm to the browser: document 10 000 times (Window_document), createElement 7 500 times (three each: Window_document again, Document_createElementChecked, Node_wrap for the pin and the interface), createTextNode 2 500 (two), appendChild 10 000, lastChild 5 000, removeChild 2 500, and the collection's Node_unpin for each of the 10 000 wrappers it frees.

partshare of the script stagems a frame (of ~37)what is in it
the collection the DOM asks for after the task (js_after_task)36 to 38 %~14the prologue that moves every node wrapper to its tree's group (half of it: one Node_treeRoots over all wrappers, a hash table of their ancestors in the browser, a reference taken and dropped on each), the finalizers (Node_unpin, destroy_subtree, the wrappers' memory), the trial deletion of the host references (a hash table of every referenced cell)
making the wrappers (wj_wrap_node)~15 %~5.5Node_wrap, the engine object and its Obj, the handle table, joining the document's group
the DOM's own work in the browser~12 %~4.5pre_insert and its hooks (scripts, links, media the insertion may start), create_element (2 %: a Unicode lower-casing through a string builder), the journal, the pins
the interpreter, property lookups up the prototype chains, argument conversionsthe rest~13
the crossings themselves~4 %~1.5a getter that crosses costs what one that does not costs, ~25 ns apart (firstChild of a leaf 300 ns, nodeType 274 ns, a JavaScript call 115 ns): the call from the interpreter into a native function is the price of a DOM call, not the trip to the browser

The engine's epoch callback (the chrome's preemption, shell_preempt) shows in 12 % of these samples; the sampler and the epoch ticker both tick every millisecond, so that share is the bias already noted above, not work.

So a command buffer in the realm's memory (mutations recorded and applied in one pass, node indices reserved ahead, names as atoms) would save the crossings, about 4 % of the stage, and keep everything else; the collection was more than a third of it. Round 3 fixed that instead (below).

#3. Scrolling a long page (p10k, 3 wheel notches every 16 ms)

167 to 177 frames/s (headless: one frame per input, the input's rate). CPU per frame 0.54 ms mean, 0.31 p50, 1.0 p95: building the chrome 0.12, page paint 0.017, style 0.002, no layout. GPU draw 0.43 ms p50, 0.73 p95; present 0.06 ms. 44 to 100 ms of CPU a second.

Bottleneck: none near a budget; the GPU's draw (0.43 ms) is the longest stage, then the chrome's build.

#4. A CSS animation (examples/site/animations.html, 123 elements)

60 frames/s, paced by the display (Wait 15.8 ms a frame). CPU per frame 0.72 ms mean, 0.56 p50: style 0.015, layout 0.066 (incremental, every other frame), paint 0.12, chrome 0.35, present 0.13; GPU 0.39 ms. 4.7 % of a core. The loop's meter: 302 turns in 5 s, none asleep, every frame caused by the page.

Bottleneck: none; the display paces it. The chrome is half the CPU of a frame.

#5. Script <-> DOM, one change per frame on a large page (examples/site/mutation.html, ~17 000 nodes, a Wasm module changes one text every 16 ms)

Before: CPU per frame 2.8 ms mean, 4.7 to 5.8 p95; the layout-shift scan (timeline_layout_shift_check) was 29 % of the window thread's work, the Largest Contentful Paint scan (timeline_present) 15 %, both walking all 16 000 boxes per mutated frame. After the change below: 1.7 to 2.1 ms mean, 2.8 to 3.8 p95; the layout-shift scan 7.5 %. The loop: 350 turns in 5 s, 165 of them after a sleep, 207 frames for a task and 184 asked.

After round 2 (medians of 5 interleaved runs): CPU work per frame 1.70 -> 1.08 ms mean, 3.23 -> 1.72 p95; the Largest Contentful Paint scan 0.2 to 0.48 -> 0.06 to 0.10 ms a frame (24 to 29 % -> 11 to 18 % of the sampled work), the walks after a style pass 2.6 to 4.6 % -> 0.2 to 0.6 %. #What changed, round 1

  1. The frame pacer books no slot for a frame it does not pace (src/browser/pacing.odin, pacer_wait). A headless window that a client waits on makes its frames at once; each one moved the next slot of platform.Frame_Slots a period on, so the first paced frame after a burst of 40 waited 40 periods with the loop's tasks queued behind it. Now such a frame resets the slot (cadence.slots.next_ns = 0). Load of p10k from the navigation: 1055 -> 34 ms. It also shortens every headless test and every wren ctl / CDP navigation in a headless Wren.
  2. The layout-shift scan reads flat arrays (src/page/timeline_lcp.odin, Ls_Boxes; lay.box_border in src/layout/query.odin). It was box_of_view and geometry_of_rects for every box and a hash table of every box built per scan; now the border rect comes from the box and its space's offset, and the last scan's rects are two flat arrays indexed by the node's handle index, swapped after each scan, an entry valid when its scan number is the last one. Mutation page: 2.6 -> 2.1 ms CPU per frame (mean of means of 5 runs; p95 4.7 -> 3.8), its share of the work 29 % -> 7.5 %.
  3. Tried and reverted: the same fast path in the Largest Contentful Paint scan (lcp_candidate_of): no difference that five runs could tell from the noise.

#What changed, round 2

Items 1, 3, 4 and 5 of round 1's list. Each measured against the build before it, 3 to 5 runs each; the share of a function is from WREN_SAMPLE=1 WREN_SAMPLE_STACK=1 WREN_SAMPLE_UNDER=<function> (the samples with it on the stack), since frame times on this machine move by a factor of 2 with its other programs. wrentool bench perf -Runs n now runs a scenario n times and prints the medians.

  1. Removed nodes go back when they double the document (src/page/js_realm.odin, js_after_task). A node a script made lives as long as its wrapper, and wrappers are freed only by a collection of the engine, which counts its own heap and not the nodes. After a script task, when the document's live nodes are twice what they were after the last collection the DOM asked for (JS_GC_NODES_GROWTH, from JS_GC_NODES_FLOOR nodes), the page asks for one: the dropped wrappers unpin their nodes, the detached trees go, their handle indices are reused, and every array indexed by node stays the document's size. nodes10k: 580 000 to 930 000 styled entries -> 10 000 to 20 000, 1.3 GB -> 307 MB, layout 29 -> 13 ms, 27 -> 34 frames/s (5 runs of each build interleaved). A growth of 8 instead of 2 was worse (16.9 frames/s): fewer, longer collections, and arrays four times larger. This is not yet "as soon as no script holds the node": that needs wrappers freed by reference counting (next, item 1).
  2. Style: the threads' arenas kept, inheriting by runs (src/style/parallel.odin thread_arena_take / thread_arena_give / thread_arena_begin, src/style/props.odin inherited_runs). Each parallel task of a full pass or of a partial restyle mapped a growing arena and the next full pass freed them all (NtFreeVirtualMemory, 10 % of the style stage); now the engine keeps them (Engine.spare_arenas, at most style.recycle_bytes of them), one reserved block each committed as it fills, and the thread that takes one empties it (the zeroing shared by the style threads; emptying them on the window's thread first cost as much as the frees). A child inherits by copying the inherited properties' bytes in runs joined across padding, not property by property. nodes10k: style 6.2 to 7.5 -> 4.5 ms a frame on the window's thread, a full pass 12 -> 6 ms; build_style on the window's thread 0.26-0.32 -> 0.19-0.25 ms a frame from the runs alone. Not done: splitting Computed (2 808 bytes, copied whole from the initial style for every element).
  3. Element Timing visits the elements that ask for it; the LCP scan skips what cannot win (src/page/timeline_lcp.odin, Document.timed in src/dom/dom.odin). The document lists the elements given an elementtiming attribute (set and cloned attributes; the reader drops the stale ones), and Element Timing visits only them; it ran on every box of every changed or scrolled frame. The Largest Contentful Paint scan settles a box from its border box clamped to the viewport (lay.box_border, the layout's arrays) when that is no larger than the largest candidate so far, before the candidate's checks. Mutation page: 0.2 to 0.48 -> 0.06 to 0.10 ms a frame; what remains is box_border itself (57 % of the scan: a read of each box's struct). Scrolling p10k cost nothing measurable before or after: its scan stops at the first input and the page has no elementtiming.
  4. The walks after a style pass driven by what changed (src/page/images.odin images_sync, css_images_sync; src/page/fonts.odin fonts_sync; Styled.image_records in src/style/cascade.odin). images_sync finds image elements in the subtrees the mutation journal says were inserted and in the elements whose attributes changed (the whole document only when the journal does not cover the change). css_images_sync does nothing when no style made since has a URL image and none was in use (the passes count the records they make with one); after partial restyles it reads the records the style journal names, unless one of them, or a node that left the tree, may have been the last user of a URL (css_users, a bit per node). fonts_sync looks only while a face is not loaded, then at the restyled elements. nodes10k: 0.6 -> 0.02 to 0.035 ms a frame (1.2 -> 0.2 % of the work); mutation page 2.6 to 4.6 % -> 0.2 to 0.6 %.

#Round 3: the locks of the loop and the network, measured against lock-free queues

Item 7 of round 2's list. The locks of src/host, src/net and src/fetch, and of what posts between them and the loop, as producers and consumers:

lockproducesconsumeshow oftenheld for
host/loop.odin Loop.muany thread posts a task (network drains, blocking jobs' completions, image decoders, the page thread, workers' links)the loop thread, once a turnevery post: thousands a second during a loadan append; the turn's swap of the arrays
net/client.odin Client.muWinHTTP's threads (headers, each chunk of read_chunk bytes, done, failed)the loop, one posted drain per burstevery network eventan append; the drain's swap
net/websocket.odin Ws_Manager.muWinHTTP's threads (frames, writes done, close)the loop, one ws_drain per burstevery WebSocket eventan append; the swap
host/thread_pool.odin mu + condparallel_for (style passes, a few a frame)the pool's threadsevery roundthree stores; the helpers' wake-up
host/blocking.odin Blocking_Pool.mu + 2 condsthe loop (run_blocking)4 workerseach blocking job (file reads, hashing): tens a secondan append; ordered_remove(0)
host/thread.odin live_mua thread starting or endingthe teardown's reportper threadan append
host/shutdown.odin sd.muthe teardown's stepsits watchdogper step of a teardowna copy of a name
fetch/blob_urls.odin blob_store.muURL.createObjectURL, revokeObjectURL (any App's thread)a load of a blob: URLper blob URLa map lookup

The built-in network stack (network.backend = rust) queues its events in the library (native/) and posts one rust_drain when its queue stops being empty: nothing of ours to lock.

Decision: the mutexes stay. Two lock-free designs of the loop's queue were built and measured against Loop.mu (the commits "The event loop and the network take no lock" and "The loop's queue, second design", kept in the history): neither moved as many posts a second through a running loop from one thread, and the consumer was not faster; the latency of a post was the same. The network's inboxes used the same queue (same verdict: they gain nothing at network rates and lose the same way in a burst from one thread), and parallel_for's round handed over by one atomic word was slower than the mutex and condition (0.53 against 0.36 us a round). What was kept: the tests and the two benches.

  1. First design: blocks of slots claimed by a compare-and-swap on the tail, the consumer popping one slot at a time. Four producers fought for the tail (10 M/s against the mutex's 25), and the consumer ran a third as fast.
  2. Second design: a wait-free fetch-and-add claim; blocks found by number from a hint and linked by the first producer that needs one, retired with the tail's position when the consumer leaves them (a producer that may still hold one claimed before that mark: once the consumer has taken every position before it, the block is free to use again); the consumer walking the slots in place up to the position its turn began at; slots and the queue's fields on lines of their own; the wake left pending while work keeps coming, cleared only at the end of a turn that left nothing (so producers write nothing to it during a turn), and a call to the system only when the loop sleeps. Four producers now match the mutex. One producer does not: the loop, faster than the producer, catches up with it every 2 or 3 tasks (about 400 000 turns per million posts, against 11 000 to 17 000 with the mutex, which made the loop wait while the producer appended), and every catching-up moves the queue's lines between the two cores and slows the producer. Batching that away means making the loop wait for work it could run: a latency the mutex does not have.

post_rate_and_latency (src/host/loop_test.odin) and parallel_for_round_cost (src/host/thread_test.odin), -Perf, -o:speed, the mutex and the second design, 7 runs each alternated; the median, range in brackets:

mutexlock-free (second design)
1 million posts through the running loop, 1 thread24.0 M/s (23.5-42.9)14.6 M/s (13.4-17.4)
the same, 4 threads at once20.6 M/s (19.7-29.7)21.4 M/s (20.9-36.5)
one thread posting, the loop not running38.4 M/s (36.2-42.1)34.4 M/s (30.8-38.0)
the loop running them alone198 M/s (162-204)172 M/s (137-213)
post to run on a waiting loop, median / 99th0.3 / 0.7 us0.3 / 0.7 us

The browser (wrentool bench perf, profile builds of the mutex and of the first design, headless, 3 runs of each alternated; the median, range in brackets) could not tell them apart either: p10k_load 311 (257-411) against 255 (251-740) ms to load; mutation 75.5 (71.6-86.2) against 73.5 (72.4-104.5) frames/s; js_nodes10k 47.2 (43.9-47.9) against 44.8 (44.4-47.0) frames/s. A post costs tens of nanoseconds either way, and a browser posts thousands a second.

What would change the verdict: a measured stall of the loop behind a producer descheduled with the lock held (the frame timeline would show a turn that waited on Loop.mu); none has been seen.

#What changed, round 3: style and layout

Items 2 and 3 of round 2's list, and the profiler (item 8) to see the threads where the work now is. Measured as in round 2: 5 runs of each build interleaved (wrentool bench perf, one scenario after the other with each build in turn), and the shares of the samples.

  1. Computed split by group (src/style/types.odin Group, src/style/props.odin). What few elements set is in six groups behind a pointer each, with using, so every read is unchanged (c.transform): the background layers (240 bytes), transforms (184), transitions and animations (224), grid (256), masks (128), and the rest (effects, counters, containment, container queries, scrolling, anchors: 280). A style shares the groups of the initial values, built once in read-only pages, until it sets a property of one; the cascade then copies that group once for the element (cx_take, called by apply_prop and the inherit / initial / unset copies); code that writes into a style elsewhere (the timeline's overlays and transitions, keyframes, scratch styles of interpolation, layout's anchored boxes) takes its own copy first (prop_take). A write into a group that is not one's own changes every style that shares it: into the initial values it faults at once, which is how the tests found the two that did. The comparisons (computed_equal, layout_equal, the layout journal's runs) skip a group the two styles share. An element's style is 1 544 bytes instead of 2 808, plus the groups it sets. nodes10k: 20.1 -> 11.1 MB of styles a full pass, the pass 9.4 -> 8.8 ms, 302 -> 275 MB; mutation pages 13.5 -> 7.7 MB a pass, partial restyles 5 to 12 % faster; p10k loaded: 13.5 -> 7.7 MB. The style threads zero the arena they take back (arena_free_all, 13 % of their samples on nodes10k): half the bytes now. No group holds an inherited property: inheriting still copies the inherited properties' bytes (about 500 of the 1 544, see Next).
  2. The layout thread's heap growth (src/browser/page_thread.odin). With the profiler able to see it (below), the growing dynamic arrays of round 1 are gone from the page thread (round 2's node lifetime fixed them: the arrays indexed by node stay the document's size). What was left: its temporary memory. The runtime's temporary arena keeps only its first block (4 MB); a layout pass of nodes10k needs more, so every pass mapped more blocks and free_all gave them back (NtFreeVirtualMemory, 2.7 to 3.2 % of the thread, and fresh pages faulted in at the next pass). The page thread now keeps one block as large as its largest pass needed (times 5/4, up to 512 MB), emptied after each: NtFreeVirtualMemory 0 % of its samples.
  3. Partial restyle on nodes10k: measured, not changed. Every frame inserts 7 500 new elements: a partial restyle restyles them all, as a full pass does, and leaves the old records in the arena (a full pass every sixth frame for "memory left by partial restyles"). Allowed (style.incremental.max_ratio=1), a partial restyle costs 8.9 ms against 8.3 for a full pass, and the style stage per frame is the same; layout is a full pass either way. What a restyle of new elements costs is the cost of styling an element (matching, building the style), which item 1 lowered.
  4. The profiler samples the threads that run (src/browser/prof.odin, other_sampler_proc): each millisecond the thread with the most CPU cycles since its last sample (QueryThreadCycleTime, handles kept open), so a thread is sampled in proportion to its CPU time; per thread, the functions anywhere on its stack. nodes10k: the page thread 160 -> 1 900 samples in 15 s; the main sampler, which it counted as the busiest thread, is left out.

#What changed, round 3: the script stage

The script stage of nodes10k, measured first (the table in section 2), then the largest part of it.

  1. A wrapper that carries nothing of its own is in no group (native/js/odin/wj/qjs_platform.odin, wrapper_plain, gc_prologue). Every node wrapper was a member of its tree's group, the document's included, so every collection's prologue placed every wrapper (a reference taken and dropped on each, the browser walking every wrapper's ancestors through a hash table) and the trial deletion counted them all. A wrapper with no listener, no [SameObject] value, no data of the engine, no own property, its interface's prototype, extensible, and never a WeakMap / WeakSet key, a WeakRef or FinalizationRegistry target (OBJ_HELD_WEAKLY in src/engine/jsrt, JS_IsUntouched) can go when no script holds it, connected or not, and be made again, the same, when a script reaches its node: nothing tells the two apart. It joins a group only when its tree is detached and has a group (holding any wrapper of a detached tree must keep the others), and new wrappers start in none (only a collection frees, and its prologue places them). The prologue crosses for the other wrappers alone, and for the plain ones only when some detached tree has a group. Test: js_plain_wrappers_go_the_others_stay_the_same (web_realm.odin).
  2. The trial deletion of host references without a hash table (src/engine/jsrt/gc.odin gc_mark_ext, host_class.odin host_mark_value): the counts are subtracted in the cells themselves and put back from a flat array.
  3. Element names lower-cased in ASCII (src/dom/dom.odin create_element, lower_name): DOM's createElement and getElementsByTagName ask for ASCII lower case; the Unicode lower-casing went through a string builder rune by rune (2 % of the script stage). WPT dom/nodes: 27 subtests better (case.html, createElement("İnput"), getElementsByTagName of non-ASCII names); one worse, case.html's getElementsByTagName a:Ä, which compares names the way the other a: cases of that file already got wrong.

#What changed, round 4: layout of DOM-heavy pages

Item 3 of round 3's list. Measured as in round 3 (wrentool bench perf, the base and the new profile build in turn, 5 runs each; the median, range in brackets) and with the profiler on the page thread (WREN_SAMPLE_THREADS=1).

  1. Column balancing: measured, not changed. Counted on nodes10k (2 500 list items in six columns): a multi-column container lays its content out once per pass (layout_multicol already lays it out in one strip and cuts it: gather_units, place_units), and balancing tries 4 heights, each a walk of the 2 500 units in their flat array: 0.05 ms of a 2.3 ms block layout. Laying the content out again is left to what forces it (a nested container that crosses a column, MC_NEST_TRIES). What the 36 % of the page thread in the multi-column layout was: the paragraphs in the columns laid out on the page thread alone. A page with columns turned frames_on on, and a pass with frames ran without the layout threads. Now a full pass whose frames are all horizontal (columns, no vertical writing mode) lays its simple paragraphs out ahead on the threads like any other page (pre_run, parallel.odin): the width prediction goes into the columns (pre_widths: a column's width, a spanner the container's), and the flows are marked before the threads start (flows_mark: mark_flow writes flags of the boxes the threads read). Incremental passes and vertical frames keep one thread. nodes10k: 2 501 of 2 501 paragraphs laid out ahead and taken; the block layout's step 2.64 -> 1.19 ms.
  2. The font of an element (font_info, context.odin; Style_Sum, style_sum.odin). The per-pass map from a 64 byte key to a font (hashing the key cost about 380 cycles a lookup, half the elements of nodes10k looked one up) and its one-entry memo are gone: a pass's fonts are a short flat list compared whole, tried after the font of the parent (near). The summaries made on the layout threads say which elements have their parent's font (Parent_Font, the keys compared there): construction then reads none of their font properties, and a text whose style is its parent element's takes that element's font (Frame.font_el, Frame.fi). Not a cache: nothing is kept from one pass to the next, the list is the pass's fonts. The summaries also carry the decorations, column-span and negative margins, which construction and mark_bfc_floats read from each style before (each a cache miss on a style made on another thread). The tree step: 1.81 -> 1.08 ms.
  3. The page thread's temporary block, as round 3 meant it (page_thread.odin): the block was set as the context's temporary allocator inside an if, and an assignment to the context lasts as long as its block: every pass ran on the runtime's own temporary arena, mapping blocks past the first and giving them back (NtFreeVirtualMemory 3 to 5 % of the page thread once the threads made the pass use more). Set at the scope of the thread's procedure, the block grew once (to 6.6 MB, then 7.4 MB a pass) in 410 passes.
  4. Smaller ones: the bounds of a box in a flow without a list on the heap (flow_bounds, once for every box and line of the flow in compute_overflow: the finish step 0.69 -> 0.35 ms); the incremental attempt adds a container as a rebuild root once, not once per child that changed (add_target: 7 500 entries of the same ul on nodes10k).
  5. Short text runs: measured, not changed. Before 1, measuring words was word_find (the toolkit's word cache), 3.6 % of the page thread; with the paragraphs on the layout threads it no longer shows on the page thread, and shaping proper (shape_run) shows only in the window thread's paint (5.7 % of Paint_Items, 1.4 ms a frame). An advance table for ASCII runs would save little here, and its exact fallback needs what the font's kerning and ligature tables do with those characters: not done.

The private memory grows by the summaries' and the predictions' temporary arrays and the layout threads' own; p10k_load, p10k_scroll and mutation move within their noise (the load of p10k by the machine's other programs, a factor of 3), and multicol.html resized makes incremental passes, which keep one thread.

#What changed, round 4: the cost of styling one element

Item 2 of round 3's list. Five profile builds measured against each other (the one before the round, then each step on top of the last), interleaved, wrentool bench perf and the sampler as in round 3.

  1. Identical styles shared (src/style/share.odin). A computed style is a value, made of: its parent's style (the record), the declarations that match the element (its matched entries: rule, selector, encapsulation context, for the element and for its styled pseudo-elements: ::before, ::after, ::selection, ::placeholder), its style attribute (by text), its encapsulation depth, and what is the same for the whole pass (the rules, the media environment, the page's color scheme, the settings). Two elements of one pass whose inputs are equal get one record: a table per pass (flat, open addressing; the keys' words in one array) maps the inputs to the record the first one got. It is not a cache: it holds the values the pass made, lives as long as that pass, is never asked about another and never invalidated, and an element it does not find costs what it cost before. What makes a style the element's own keeps it out of the table: presentational hints (attributes as declarations), a lang other than the parent's language, an element the embedder hides or that is above the top layer; a query container (its size is the element's), position-try fallbacks, a list marker that shows a counter, generated content with attr(), counters or quotes. A record in the table is never written again: what markers and generated content resolve to is resolved when it is made, and the counters' walks write a value only when it differs. So a record no longer says whose it is: Styled.nodes holds the element of each slot (what style_of checks against a recycled index), and layout's refresh (layout/refresh.odin) re-points an element's inline items by the element, not by the record its old record became for some box (the demo pages' random mutations found a link left with the record of a block that had shared its style). A partial restyle that finds the style it made equal to the one in force puts that one in the table and drops what it made, as before. Tests: src/style/share_test.odin (one record for equal inputs; two for a style attribute, an attribute read by attr(), lang, :hover, the container of a query or of cq units that differ; numbered markers). nodes10k: 11.1 -> 0.2 MB of styles a pass, the style stage 8.8 (8.0-9.1) -> 7.6 (7.4-8.0) ms, 47.7 -> 52.9 frames/s; mutation_fullstyle 5.1 -> 2.0 ms a pass (best runs 4.2 -> 1.9), 15.3 -> 0.3 MB; p10k loaded 7.7 -> 3.2 MB.
  2. The inherited properties in a group of their own (Inherited_Group, src/style/types.odin), shared with the parent until the element sets one: an element that sets none inherits by one pointer (it copied about 500 bytes, inherit_all, now gone). The cascade takes the group on the first write (cx_take, cx_own): apply_prop, the inherit / initial / unset copies (a copy from the parent whose group it shares is nothing to do), and the derived values, written only when they differ: scheme_settle, the legacy white-space, the content language, the monospace size, text-combine-upright out of a vertical mode. Outside the cascade: the timeline's push_inherited and pseudo_inherit and derive_fields take their own copy; layout's anonymous boxes share their parent's (the border-spacing they copied again was the same value and is no longer written). The initial inherited values follow the preferences: one group per style pass (and per configuration for validating declarations), not read-only pages. An element's style is 1 KB instead of 1.5. nodes10k: no change (its styles were shared already); p10k loaded 3.2 -> 2.7 MB a pass; mutation_fullstyle 0.3 -> 0.2 MB, the pass the same within the noise (best runs 1.9 -> 1.7 ms).
  3. The style arenas emptied without zeroing (style_arena_allocator, style_arena_empty, src/style/cascade.odin). A virtual arena zeroes what it held when it is emptied, so that what it hands out next is zero: the computed styles and their groups, which the cascade overwrites whole, were zeroed twice. The style threads' arenas and the pass's own are now emptied by resetting their block; what is allocated from them is zeroed when it is handed out, except the records and the groups (record_new, group_take). On nodes10k the zeroing was 13 % of the style threads because each pass made 11 MB: after item 1 it makes 0.1 MB and the zeroing was gone already. mutation_fullstyle: arena_free_all 1.6 % of the busiest style thread's samples -> none (the allocator 2.4 %); the pass the same within the noise.
  4. A restyle of mostly new elements gives up before marking them (inserted_exceed, src/style/restyle_dom.odin). On nodes10k every frame tried a partial restyle first, marked what the 10 000 journal entries reach (the invalidation index, the sibling walks), estimated the work, and found it too much: that marking cost twice the full pass that followed (half of the style stage's samples, mark_mutations). The elements of the inserted subtrees are restyled whole, so their count is a lower bound of the estimate: past the limit, the answer is the one the marking would give (documents without shadow trees; not with WREN_RESTYLE_TRACE, which reports the marks). nodes10k: the style stage 7.6 (7.3-7.9) -> 3.3 (3.0-3.4) ms a frame, 52.2 -> 56.8 frames/s, CPU work per frame 54.9 -> 50.7 ms.

What was measured on the other pages, before the round and after it (medians, ranges in brackets): mutation and mutation_class above (map, 5); examples/site/modern-css.html resized (240 full passes a run, 5 runs of each build): 0.95 (0.95-1.01) -> 0.96 (0.95-1.84) ms a pass, 0.2 MB, CPU work per frame 0.40 -> 0.39 ms; p10k loaded (5 runs of each): 240 (238-280) -> 241 (240-776) ms to load, its full pass 6 (6-7) -> 6 (5.5-13.5) ms, 7.7 -> 2.7 MB of styles. The machine ran other agents' builds meanwhile: single runs moved by a factor of 2 to 3, hence the ranges.

#What changed, round 5: matching, the walks in tree order, the incremental attempt

Items 2 and 3 of round 4's list. The base and the new profile build in turn (wrentool bench perf), 5 runs each on a quiet machine; the shares are the sampler's (WREN_SAMPLE_STACK=1 WREN_SAMPLE_THREADS=1), on profile builds of both.

  1. Matching shared between siblings and cousins (src/style/sibling_match.odin). Two sibling elements with the same tag and the same attributes look up the same entries of the index, pass the same ancestor filter, and every part of a selector matched against an ancestor answers the same for both: what can tell them apart is only what a selector asks of the element itself beyond its tag and attributes (its position among its siblings, a sibling combinator to its left, its state, its content, :has(), :scope). Such an entry is own (Entry.own, from the selector when the index is built, selector_deps). Cousins (children of alike parents, up to a common ancestor) differ besides by what a selector asks the same way of an ancestor or of an ancestor's sibling (Entry.above). The walk in tree order keeps, for each depth, a family: the children of one parent or of alike parents, and for each kind of element in it (up to SIB_FAMILY_KINDS) the first one, matched in full, with the entries it matched and those the others must try again (with its answer). The next element of a kind takes them, matching again only own entries, and above ones for a cousin; its lists are those a full match gives, in the same order, so the share table (round 4) then finds its style. Full passes, the style threads and the restyle walk use it (an element a partial restyle passes without matching it starts a family of its own below it: sib_pass_by); documents with shadow trees do not (the flat tree's siblings may come from different trees). Not a cache: it holds what this pass matched for elements before, is dropped when the walk meets another family at that depth, and nothing in it outlives the pass or is invalidated. Test: sibling_match_test.odin (on a page with every kind of selector that tells alike elements apart, each element's lists against a full match, hovered elements and parents included, and how many took their matching from another). On mutation_fullstyle, collect_entries was 44 to 53 % of the busiest style threads' samples, and is 1.5 %; what matching is left is the entries matched again (match_chain 12 to 21 %: the browser's own :disabled, :focus-visible, :popover-open and :fullscreen reach every element, and :disabled asks the forms model).
  2. No counter walk when no box shows a counter (counters_tally, src/style/counters.odin). After a parallel pass the counters and quotes are resolved by a walk in tree order. It writes only what a box shows (numbered markers, counter() and quotes in content) and says whether a counter is used (counters_used, which partial restyles read). The style threads now count, of the boxes shown, those that show a counter or a quote and those that change one: with none of the first, the walk has nothing to write and its answer is whether any of the second exists. nodes10k (bullets, and the ul that resets list-item) needs no walk. Test: parallel_pass_counters_without_the_walk.
  3. The check of what was inserted, flat (inserted_exceed, src/style/restyle_dom.odin): the inserted nodes are bits by handle index (set for live handles only: the index of a node that went may be another node's), a second set keeps a node inserted twice from counting twice, and one walk up from each node stops at an inserted ancestor or finds the document; it was a hash set, a walk up to find whether the node is connected and another to find an inserted ancestor. With 2 and 3 the window thread's share of the style stage of nodes10k: compute_styles itself (with the walk inlined) 112 -> 57 samples, inserted_exceed 61 + connected 20 -> 35, the stage 1 139 -> 608 samples in runs of the same length.
  4. The incremental attempt decides from the removed boxes first (removed_boxes, src/layout/incremental.odin). Every box of an element the journal says was removed is made again with its subtree, as a plan of its own or inside a container rebuilt whole: their count is a lower bound of what the attempt would find, and past the limit the attempt gives up before looking for what to rebuild (add_target, touched_ancestor, plan_children, quadratic in the children of one container, subtree_size). A bit per box marks those of removed elements, so a subtree inside another counts once; one inside a replaced element is left out (its container is laid out again, not rebuilt). nodes10k: what the page thread did besides its full pass (layout_document less run_full, nearly all of it that search) was 23 % of its samples, 0.3 % now. Test: inc_removed_boxes_decide_first.
  5. Measured, not kept. The display list of a flow (push_flow_item copied a Space of hundreds of bytes and every fragment for each item; emit_lines read visibility and pointer-events from each text's style where the box's flags hold them when the box has the text's style): rewritten without the copies and reads, the display step of nodes10k was 0.63 (0.60-1.21) ms before and 0.67 (0.62-0.76) after; the compiler loaded only the fields used, and the styles read are the few shared records, in cache. The page thread's temporary block emptied without zeroing (what is allocated zeroed when handed out instead): the window thread's wait on layout 3.32 (3.24-3.48) against 3.30 (3.28-3.32) ms without it (6 runs each), the same bytes zeroed at another time.

#What changed, round 6: the script stage of DOM-heavy pages

Item 1 of round 5's list. Profiled first: the engine's own samples (jspage -image <engine built with buildjs -names> -profile: Wasmtime's guest profiler, a sample at each epoch tick), the browser's side with WREN_SAMPLE_STACK=1 WREN_SAMPLE_UNDER=page::run_animation_frames. The guest profiler takes its sample where Wasm code checks the epoch (function entries, loop heads): the time of a call into the browser is counted to the first function the engine enters after it returns (JS_DupValue after Node_preInsert, libc_free after Node_unpin, wj_wrap_node after Document_createElementChecked), which the shares below take into account. Each change was measured on its own with a timed copy of nodes10k in jspage (the time of the page's build() a frame, p50 of 400 frames; for the collection, a timer around js.collect in a build of jspage that was not kept), the build before it and the build with it in turn, 3 runs each; then the browser (wrentool bench perf, 5 runs of each build, interleaved, the order turning).

  1. Document and Window objects are plain platform objects (class_kind_of, src/tools/bindgen/jsgen/jsgen.odin). An interface with a named property getter in its IDL got the named class, whose own-property hook runs on every read of a property the object does not hold itself: every document.createElement asked it (through the C API's bridge), and the interpreter's fast path gives up on any object with an exotic hook. The glue implements no named getter for Document, Window (nor XMLDocument, TouchEvent): the hook could only answer "none". The class is now named only when the glue implements the getter on the interface or one it inherits from (Storage, DOMStringMap). build() 18.8 (18.8-19.1) -> 17.3 (17.2-17.3) ms.
  2. A wrapper's interface by the name's first byte, then the name (emit_name_switch, src/tools/bindgen/jsgen/outputs.odin; js_html_interface, js_svg_interface): a switch on strings compares them one after the other: 58 comparisons for li, 90 for span (string_eq under Node_wrap, 2 % of the window thread's script stage). 17.6 (17.5-17.6) -> 16.6 (16.6-16.6) ms. Test: element_interface_by_name.
  3. The insertion steps in one walk (inserted_kinds, src/page/js_load.odin). Every insertion walked the inserted subtree three times (style sheets, media elements, scripts and frames), each with a list of its own; one walk now notes which of those names the subtree holds, and only the steps that found something look further. 16.6 (16.3-16.6) -> 15.7 (15.6-15.8) ms. Test: inserted_subtree_kinds.
  4. The wrapper's platform object in the engine's block (JS_NewObjectProtoClassPayload, src/engine/jscapi; Host_Object.payload, src/engine/jsrt/host_class.odin). A wrapper took three allocations: the object (the engine's size classes), its host part (new through the engine's general allocator) and the glue's Obj (libc_calloc), and its finalizer freed the last two. The host part is now a block of the size classes that holds the Obj after it, freed with the object. 15.8 (15.6-16.1) -> 14.4 (14.0-15.0) ms. Test: judge capi (payloads zeroed, one per object, a cycle through them collected, 10 000 made and dropped without the heap keeping them).
  5. The C API reads a value without decoding it (cell_of, object_of, src/engine/jscapi/types.odin): JS_DupValue, JS_FreeValue, JS_GetOpaque, JS_SetOpaque, JS_GetClassID built a whole engine value out of the word (a switch over every tag) to read a pointer, and JS_DupValue copied the Odin context for every value, a number too. The collection the DOM asks for calls them for every wrapper (its prologue's obj_of, gc_mark, the finalizers): 8.1 (7.0-8.3) -> 5.8 (5.8-5.8) ms a collection; build() 14.1 (14.0-14.2) -> 13.3 (13.2-13.3) ms.
  6. A getter is called where the lookup found it (get_field in src/engine/jsrt/interp.odin, global_get in globals.odin): a DOM attribute (lastChild) was found on the prototype chain, given up as not a data property, looked up again by get_property, then called; a global accessor (document, [LegacyUnforgeable] and so the window's own) went through [[HasProperty]] and [[Get]] after the slot lookup that had found it. 13.3 (13.1-13.5) -> 12.6 (12.5-12.8) ms.
  7. Measured, not kept. destroy_subtree (the browser frees each tree the collection unpins) with a list of inline capacity instead of a heap list per call: 8.10 against 8.28 ms a collection, build() the same (the destruction is the nodes' own memory: their names and texts, the pool).

#What changed, round 7: the script stage of DOM-heavy pages, what was left

Item 1 of round 6's list, measured as round 6 did: the engine's samples (the guest profiler in jspage, its bias noted there: the finalizers' Node_unpin showed as libc_free, 13 % of the samples, Node_preInsert as JS_DupValue), the browser's under page::run_animation_frames and under each import (WREN_SAMPLE_UNDER). Each change was timed in jspage on a copy of nodes10k (build() a frame, p50 of 400 frames; the collection with a timer around js.collect in a build of jspage that was not kept), the build before it and the build with it in turn, 4 to 8 runs each; then the browser, all of it (6 runs of each build, interleaved).

  1. A collection unpins its nodes in one call (unpin_later, gc_epilogue, native/js/odin/wj/qjs_platform.odin; JS_SetGCEpilogue, src/engine/jscapi; Host_Config.gc_epilogue, src/engine/jsrt). A finalized node wrapper called the browser's Node_unpin, one call for each of the 10 000 wrappers a collection frees; their handles now go into a flat array and the epilogue, called at the end of every collection and at the runtime's teardown, hands them to Node_unpinAll (which, as Node_unpin did, runs nothing when it returns: hold_reactions). The collection 5.45 (5.20-6.03) -> 4.98 (4.90-6.24) ms. Test: judge capi (the epilogue once a collection, after its finalizers).
  2. The string arguments of the bindings read in place (JS_ToStringView, src/engine/jscapi/misc.odin; STR_VIEW, native/js/odin/wj). Every string argument was copied to the C heap (JS_ToCStringLen2: an UTF-8 copy in a fresh block) and freed after the call. A string that is all ASCII is its own UTF-8: the generated bindings, whose imports read the bytes before the native returns while the caller holds the argument, and createElement, now pass its bytes where they are (a rope is flattened first; any other string is copied as before). build() 12.35 (12.34-13.68) -> 11.08 (10.98-11.47) ms. Test: judge capi (ASCII, a concatenation; no view of Latin-1, UTF-16, a number, an object).
  3. Element names are the program's strings (STATIC_NAMES, static_name, set_name, src/dom/names.odin; Node.name_static). create_element copied each name to the heap (half of the browser's createElement, under RtlAllocateHeap) and the destruction of the tree freed it. A name of the HTML elements, the older ones the parser meets, or SVG's and MathML's most used (by first letter, at most NAME_STATIC_MAX bytes) is now the program's string, shared by every element of that name and its clones; any other is copied as before. build() 11.06 (10.97-11.22) -> 10.62 (10.53-10.69) ms. Test: element_names_static_or_copied (the test runner's allocator reports a static name freed or a copy leaked).
  4. The wrappers of nodes in an array by handle index (Node_Table, qjs_platform.odin). The glue found a node's wrapper through a hash table (open addressing, a backward shift on every delete: 10 000 deletes a collection); a node handle is its pool slot's index and generation, so the wrapper now sits at the index, the full handle in the entry telling a node from the one that had the slot before. A handle whose entry is taken (a node of another document, a slot reused while the old wrapper waits for a collection) goes to the hash table, empty otherwise. The collection 4.30 (4.23-5.45) -> 3.55 (3.53-3.74) ms; build() the same.
  5. Measured, not kept. A flag per interface saying whether it or one it inherits from has [LegacyUnforgeable] members, so that a new wrapper does not walk its five interfaces to find none (wj_define_unforgeables, 1.4 % of the engine's samples): build() 10.81 (10.60-11.29) against 10.68 (10.63-12.29) ms, 10 runs each. The document getter crosses to the browser on every read (Window_document, 10 000 times a frame, 2 % of the engine's samples): keeping the realm's document in the glue would assume the page's document never changes under a realm, which adopt_document does not promise; not done.

#What changed, round 8: layout of DOM-heavy pages, what a full style pass costs per page

Items 2 and 3 of round 7's list. Profiled first on the page thread and the style threads (WREN_SAMPLE_THREADS=1 WREN_SAMPLE_STACK=1, in a build that listed more of each thread's functions, not kept), and on the window thread under style::compute_styles (WREN_SAMPLE_UNDER); then the base and the new profile build in turn (wrentool bench perf, 5 runs each, the order turning; median, range in brackets). The steps of a full layout pass (tree, layout, finish, display, bands, p50 of each) tell the changes of layout apart.

What nodes10k's page thread did (1 052 samples while running, the base): the block layout 26 % (the 2 500 list items in columns, layout_multicol: the items themselves, their paragraphs taken from the threads, the columns cut), the display list 19 %, building the box tree 16 %, finishing 15 % (the overflow of each box and line of the flow, flow_bounds_add 6 %), the bands 5 %, the walks of writing modes around the block layout 4 %, copying the predictions of the layout threads 2 %.

  1. The display list of a page with columns on the layout threads (build_display_list, push_flow_item, flows_clip_free). A page with columns turned frames_on on and its display list was made on the page thread alone: an item of a flow becomes one copy for each column it shows in, and push_flow_item appended them to the layout's list whatever share was making them. They now go to the share's own list, as the other items do; a clip inside a flow is made again for each column (flow_clip adds clips), so a flow that holds one keeps the display list on one thread. Layout.dl_shares says how many shares the threads made. nodes10k: the display step 0.63 (0.62-0.70) -> 0.39 (0.38-0.40) ms. Test: parallel_multicol (the columns, a box across three columns: its item in each, against one thread; a clip in the columns: one thread).
  2. No turn to physical coordinates when no frame is vertical (pre_run): after the block layout every box was visited to make it physical (frames_to_physical: a walk in tree order, the frame of each box), which with columns alone changes nothing. The predictions of the layout threads written in place (pre_predict): made in temporary arrays and copied whole into Pre_Keep (a megabyte on nodes10k), they are written there by the threads. The flows marked in box order (flows_mark): a full pass makes a parent before its children; the walk in tree order went. The layout step 1.24 (1.20-1.29) -> 1.03 (1.00-1.04) ms; the finishing step 0.35 -> 0.41 ms (the walk that went had brought the boxes into the cache for it): both together 1.59 -> 1.44 ms.
  3. The page's color scheme looked for among the document's <meta> elements (Document.metas, page_color_scheme). Every full style pass walked the whole document for <meta name="color-scheme"> on the window thread: a quarter of the window thread's style samples on mutation_fullstyle. The document lists the <meta> elements it makes (created, cloned; a freed one is dropped by the reader); those in its tree are the candidates, in tree order. Test: page_color_scheme_metas_in_tree_order (made in another order than the tree's, one never inserted, one inside another <meta>). :disabled answers at once for what is not a form control (matches_simple): the UA's :disabled reaches every element and asked the forms model (a call through the page, a switch on the name) before finding it is none. nodes10k: the style stage 1.85 (1.82-1.98) -> 1.73 (1.73-1.74) ms; mutation_fullstyle 1.28 (1.28-1.32) -> 1.21 (1.20-1.23) ms.
  4. The journal of a full pass compares a pair of records once per chunk (Diff_Pair, diff_chunk). The layout journal compares every element's old and new record (layout_level, 28 to 36 % of the busiest style threads on mutation_fullstyle, and on the window thread, which takes chunks too). Alike elements share their record in both passes (round 4), so a chunk keeps the answer of each pair it compared, by slot (JOURNAL_DIFF_PAIRS): an element whose two records are a pair already compared takes the answer. Not a cache: the pairs are of these two passes, live while the chunk is compared, and nothing in them is invalidated. mutation_fullstyle (12 runs of each build, interleaved, a busy machine; 10 of the 12 pairs went the same way): the style stage 1.65 (1.21-2.91) -> 1.10 (0.80-1.57) ms p50, a full pass 2.24 -> 1.51 ms.
  5. Measured, not kept. The bands reading each item once instead of twice (its space and vertical extent in a small array): 0.126 against 0.132 ms. The finishing step looking up a box's columns once for all its lines (flow_bounds_add finds the container's record in a map for each rect): 0.402 against 0.406 ms.

What is left on the window thread's style stage of mutation_fullstyle: flat_sizes, the walk of the whole document that weighs the subtrees before the style threads share them (compute_styles and the flat-tree steps under it, about a third of its samples).

#What changed, round 9: what a full style pass costs on the window thread, the finishing of a flow

Items 2 and 3 of round 8's list. Profiled first (WREN_SAMPLE_THREADS=1 WREN_SAMPLE_STACK=1, in a build that also listed each thread's own functions, not kept). Then, besides the browser, each change was timed in process, where a step of a pass is measured to a few microseconds: a test not kept that lays out a copy of nodes10k (2 500 items in six columns, the default settings and layout threads) 600 times, and one that styles a copy of mutation.html (10 000 elements) 600 times with seven style threads, each pass recycled as the page recycles it; the base and the new build in turn, 4 runs each, the median of each run. Then the browser (wrentool bench perf, 5 runs of each build, interleaved, the order turning; median, range in brackets).

  1. The weights of the subtrees in one walk (flat_sizes, src/style/parallel.odin). Before the style threads share the work, the window thread weighs every subtree: a walk that pushed each element, listed it in tree order, wrote its parent's index, reached each node three or four times (dom.get, the flat tree's first child and next sibling, the kind of each child) and then went over the list backwards. It is now one walk in tree order with a stack of the open elements: an element's size goes to its parent's when the walk leaves it, and a document without shadow trees follows the nodes' own links. 0.153 (0.153-0.154) -> 0.068 (0.067-0.068) ms on 10 000 elements. Test: flat_sizes_of_the_flat_tree (a shadow tree, named and default slots, their fallbacks: each element against a count by recursion over the flat tree).
  2. The slots of a recycled pass (styled_recycle, styled_make, Engine.spare_by_node). A full pass made its arrays of records by node (by_node, nodes: 16 bytes a node, 270 KB on mutation.html) on the heap and the pass it replaced freed its own: the new ones were pages to fault in, 0.056 ms of each pass on the window thread, before any element was styled. The engine keeps the arrays of the pass it recycles (as it keeps its arena, within style.recycle_bytes) and the next pass takes them, emptied; styled_size zeroes what it hands out, so no slot of an old pass is read. Test: recycled_pass_slots (the same arrays, no record of an element that left the document, every style equal to that of an engine that recycled nothing). With 1, the pass in process: 0.62 (0.62-0.66) -> 0.48 (0.48-0.48) ms.
  3. A multi-column container's record by index (Box.mc, Layout.mc_records, mc_record). Finishing looked the container's record up in a map for each box and line of its flow (flow_bounds_add), the window thread's queries likewise; the box now holds its record's index in a flat array. In process the finishing step did not move: 0.375 against 0.374 ms. Kept for the rule (an index where a table was looked up per rect): what flow_bounds_add costs is not the lookup.
  4. Measured, not kept. What finishing pays for the flow: without flow_bounds at all (a wrong result, to measure) the step is 0.15 ms shorter, about 15 ns a call for 10 000 calls; neither a binary search of the first column a rect reaches, with a stop at the first below it, nor the record by index (3) shortened it: the cost is the call's branches on each rect, not the search. The search and the walks of finishing in one (coordinates, clip owners, what is inside a fixed box), measured together: 0.383 against 0.382 ms. apply_shifts settling a paragraph only when one of its lines moved (ifc_settle, which it called for each of the 2 500 items): the layout step moved within its noise (0.76 to 0.89 ms in both builds, as the threads' paragraphs came in).

What the page thread of nodes10k does is left as round 8 found it (the browser: tree 0.92, layout 1.04, finish 0.36, display 0.39, bands 0.13 ms): each step walks boxes of 400 bytes (Box), and what it reads of each is a few fields scattered across them; the next gains there are item 4 below (what a step reads, in arrays of its own), not the steps' own code.

#What changed, round 10: what the steps of layout read, measured

Item 2 of round 9's list: the idea was that layout's steps wait on memory, walking Box records (352 bytes) for a few fields each, and would go faster with what each step reads in arrays of its own. Measured before anything was split, in process (a test not kept: a copy of nodes10k, 2 500 items in six columns, 7 505 boxes and 12 506 display items, laid out 600 times with the default layout threads, the p50 of each step; 3 runs of each build, interleaved), then in the browser (wrentool bench perf, the profile build, WREN_SAMPLE_THREADS=1 WREN_SAMPLE_STACK=1 with a listing of each thread's own functions that was not kept).

  1. Measured, not kept: the layout of Box and Display_Item. What a split into arrays can save is bounded by two builds that change only where the bytes lie: Box twice as large (352 bytes of padding at its end), and Box with its fields reordered so that what the walks of finishing, the display list and the scans read shares its first two cache lines (the tree links, flags and kind, the spaces and clips, positions and sizes, the line and item ranges). The full pass: 2.57 ms with the boxes as they are, 2.66 with them twice as large (tree +0.06, display +0.02, finish and the block layout within their noise), 2.56 reordered (every step within 0.01 ms). The scan of every box's rects (below) took 12 % longer with the boxes twice as large. Display items twice as large (256 bytes): the display step +0.06 ms (it writes them), the bands +0.008 ms (they read the rect and the space of each). With the caches emptied between passes (64 MB written before each, as a script stage would leave them) every step doubles and the builds above stay within each other's noise. The 2.6 MB of boxes fit the processor's last cache (32 MB on the machine measured): the steps are bound by their own code, not by memory, so no field moved; the profile below says where that code is.
  2. The scans of every box read the union of a flow's fragments directly (box_border, src/layout/query.odin; timeline_present, timeline_layout_shift_check, src/page/timeline_lcp.odin). After each frame that changed the document, the largest-paint scan and the layout-shift scan read the border rect of every box. For a box in a multi-column flow box_border answered "fragmented" and the scans called box_of_view (the padding and content rects, the walk up the spaces, the transform checks, and for the largest paint geometry_of_rects and the candidate's checks before the area that rules it out). It now gives the union of the fragments, flow_bounds of the border rect, which is what box_of_view gave, and the largest paint's area check rules a small box out before its candidacy is looked at. The layout-shift scan's reads in process: 0.233 (0.227-0.246) -> 0.133 (0.133-0.135) ms. Test: multicol_box_border (a box across two columns, one in one column, the container: box_border against box_of).

The browser (6 runs of each build for nodes10k, 4 for the others, interleaved, the order turning, on a quiet machine; a first series while other agents built moved single runs by a factor of 2 and was dropped). The scans run in page_prepare after the layout phase ends, under no phase of their own: the phase table leaves them out (they were counted to UI_Draw by the sampler), the CPU work per frame has them.

#What changed, round 11: the image search, the cut of a flow, the display items

Item 2 of round 10's list, in its order. Measured three ways: the sampler on the browser (WREN_SAMPLE=1 WREN_SAMPLE_STACK=1 WREN_SAMPLE_THREADS=1, WREN_SAMPLE_UNDER=<function>, 2 runs of each build: a share of the samples moves little with the machine's load); in process (a test not kept that lays out a copy of nodes10k 600 times with the default layout threads and reads every box's box_border after each pass, as the scans do; the p50 of each step, 3 to 4 runs of each build in turn, and a hash of the boxes, lines, display items and bands); then the browser, all of it (wrentool bench perf, 5 runs of each build, interleaved, the order turning). Other agents built and ran tests on the machine all along: single runs of the browser moved by a factor of 2 (a run of nodes10k at 20 or at 46 ms of CPU work a frame), so the browser's table below says only that nothing got worse; the samples and the in-process steps carry the measurements.

  1. The image elements found among those the document made (Document.images, named_add, src/dom/dom.odin; images_sync, src/page/images.odin). After each change of the document the window thread walked every subtree the journal said was inserted, looking for <img> and <input>: on nodes10k, 7 500 elements a frame for none. The document now lists the <img> and <input> elements it makes (created, cloned; a freed one dropped by the reader or when the list would grow), as it lists its <meta> ones (round 8), and the search reads that list, keeping those in its tree (shadow trees included) that are image elements; it runs only when the journal has an insertion, a removal or an attribute of an <img> or <input> (anything when the journal does not cover the change), not for a text that changed. nodes10k: images_sync 68 to 72 samples in about 1 000 frames (0.07 ms a frame, a quarter of UI_Draw's samples) -> 1 to 2. Tests: document_lists_its_image_elements (dom), images_found_among_the_documents_images (page: one inserted, one never inserted, a subtree removed, a type changed to image, an image in a shadow tree, a text changed).
  2. A box or line of a flow tried first against the column of the one before (flow_bounds_add, flow_inside, Mc_Record.apart, src/layout/multicol.odin; compute_overflow, box_border, the two scans). Finishing and the scans cut every box and line of a flow against each of the six columns. The columns of a container are bands across the flow, one after the other (apart, checked when they are made); a rect inside one band, short of its end edges, is reached by no other column and shown whole by that one. A caller walking boxes in order keeps the column the last one lay inside (near) and tries it first: one test instead of six where it holds, the full cut otherwise, which finds the column for the next. Not a cache: the index is checked against the record's range and the rect each time, and nothing is kept across passes. In process: finishing 0.318 (0.317-0.320) -> 0.267 (0.264-0.268) ms, the reads of every box's border 0.129 (0.129-0.134) -> 0.070 (0.070-0.071) ms; on the page thread, flow_bounds_add 8.8 to 9.1 % -> 6.5 to 6.6 % of the samples while running. unite inlined: without it the fast path's call cost 0.01 ms of the finishing and of the reads. Test: multicol_flow_bounds_near (every box and line of containers with a box across columns, a spanner, columns inside columns and a vertical writing mode, against the full cut).
  3. A display item of 104 bytes instead of 128 (Display_Item, src/layout/types.odin): thumb was set by nothing (a scrollbar's thumb is computed when it is drawn, scrollbar_thumb), and the decorations and the font index fill the padding. In process, the display step 0.28 -> 0.27 ms (each of 4 runs lower, by 0.005 to 0.024 ms): kept with the field that went.
  4. Measured, not kept: the block layout of the columns. Timed by part in process (timers not kept, each adding about 30 ns): of the layout step (0.72 to 0.85 ms with the layout threads' paragraphs coming in), laying out the 2 500 items 0.33 to 0.43 ms (about 150 ns an item, spread over layout_contents, the paragraph taken from the threads, block_width, the marker; none above 0.05 ms), gathering the units 0.06, balancing 0.06, moving the boxes to their columns (apply_shifts) 0.11; the rest is the threads' paragraphs. No part stands out to take. flow_children without its prefetch of the children's styles (one shared record on this page): the step within its noise (0.72 to 0.85 ms both ways, 4 runs each).
  5. Not done: item 1 of round 10's list (one crossing to create a node, pin it and name its interface): it changes the bindings' generator and the engine's glue, and the round's time went to the items above.
