#Heap lists per call on hot paths

style/timeline.odin:429-432,468 (an Element_Anim and three dynamic arrays for each element that declares a transition, on every full pass); browser/compositor.odin:321 (compute_floors: one heap array per group per rebuild) and :530 (node_items_make: one per node); the window thread's and the thread pool's temporary arenas, which give back what outgrew their first block after each frame or job (NtFreeVirtualMemory, 1 % of the window thread on nodes10k; the pool's are src/host's). Gone in round 2: the style threads' arenas mapped and freed with every pass. Gone in round 3: the layout thread's growing arrays (none in its samples since round 2) and its temporary blocks mapped and freed every pass. Most of layout and paint already use the temporary allocator or an arena.

#Next, ranked by measured cost on a bottleneck

After round 4 (item 3 of round 3's list, in part). Round 2's items 2, 3 and 8 are done (item 3 measured: a partial restyle of nodes10k costs what a full pass does); what is left of them is folded in below. Round 3 also measured round 2's item 7 as it stood (the loop's and the network's locks) and kept the mutexes; item 7 is now the job queues, to be measured the same way before anything replaces them. Round 2's item 1 is done in part: the engine traces, it counts no reference a script holds, so a plain wrapper still waits for a collection, but the collection no longer pays for it. After round 4. Round 3's item 2 is done for what it named (styles shared, the inherited group, the arenas, and the restyle that gave up too late); what styling an element still costs is item 3 below. After round 5. Round 4's item 2 is done (matching shared by alike elements, the counter walk, the check of what was inserted); of item 3, the incremental attempt is done, the display list of the flow and the page thread's temporary block were measured and left as they were (round 5, item 5); what is left of both is below.

After round 6. Round 5's item 1 is done in part (round 6: the named class, the interface by name, the insertion steps' walks, the wrapper's allocations, the C API's decoding, the getters); what is left of it is item 1 below.

After round 7. Round 6's item 1 is done in part (round 7: the collection's unpins in one call, the arguments' strings read in place, element names as the program's strings, the wrappers by handle index); what is left of it is item 1 below.

After round 8. Round 7's items 2 and 3 are done in part (round 8: the display list of a page with columns on the layout threads, the walks of writing modes and the copies around the block layout, the page's color scheme, :disabled, the journal's pairs of records); what is left of them is items 2 and 3 below.

After round 9. Round 8's items 2 and 3 are done in part (round 9: the weights of the subtrees in one walk, the slots of a recycled pass, a container's record by index); what round 9 measured of layout's steps moves item 2 below to the arrays they read (round 8's item 4 folded in); what is left of the style pass is item 3.

After round 10. Round 9's item 2 was measured before anything was split: the steps are not bound by the layout of the records (round 10, item 1); the scans of every box no longer take the long way for a box in a flow (item 2). Item 2 below is now the steps' own code.

After round 11. Round 10's item 2 is done in part (round 11: the image search from the document's list, a flow's boxes and lines cut against the column of the one before, a smaller display item); the block layout of the columns was timed by part and has nothing that stands out (round 11, item 4). Item 1 is unchanged and now first by far; item 2 below is what is left of layout.

After round 12. Round 11's item 1 is done in part (round 12: one crossing for a new node and its wrapper, the realm's document asked once, the root lists appended in place, native getters and string constants in the hot loop, the bridge's conversions in place, JS_GetAnyOpaque); what is left of it is item 1 below.

After round 13. Round 12's item 1 is done in part (round 13: the counting pass and the marking skip the wrappers that hold nothing, a detached tree freed by its links); what is left of it is item 1 below, and what round 13 found of the interpreter's code generation is item 9.

After round 14. The static C runtime measured against the dynamic one: the same (round 14, item 1). Item 3 below no longer pays for ::backdrop on every element (round 14, item 2); item 1 is unchanged.

After round 15. Round 14's item 9 is done (round 15: the hot loop calls nothing and is inlined; micro.js 14 % faster, macro.js 9 %), and with it the prototype walk without the host class's hooks of item 1. Real pages loaded from the navigation are item 10 below.

After round 16. Round 15's item 10 is done for what it named (round 16: the engine read ahead, Direct2D made ahead, textures zeroed on the GPU, the thread count of stats) and for what its measures found besides (what waits for a stylesheet goes on when it arrives); what the loads still spend is item 10 below. Item 1 is unchanged.

After round 17. Round 16's item 10 is done in part (round 17: Slug's bands from one sort per axis, the image decoder's start that waits for nothing; Slug's data made while shaping measured and not kept); what its measures found, the frame that waits for its slot before the tasks, leads item 10 below. Item 1 is unchanged.

After round 18. Round 17's item 10 is done for its first part (round 18: the loop's tasks run in the frame's wait for its slot, a first paint waits for no slot); p10k's first passes lead item 10 below. Item 1 is unchanged.

After round 19. Off this list: the licence card of about:wren under the pointer (a document changed only in style attributes is refreshed, not laid out; planes keep their raster scale; the development build lost the Direct3D debug layer).

After rounds 20, 21 and 23. Item 1's interpreter gave way to a JIT for hot loops and hot functions (round 20: loops, properties, calls; 21: whole functions, direct calls, objects, strings, DOM getters, natives; 23: document, objects allocated inline, the script's accessors): nodes10k's build() p50 8.63 -> 7.44 ms in round 23's series. What is left of item 9 now counts only for code the JIT does not take; engine/jit.md has the JIT's own list.

After rounds 22 and 24. Off this list too: what the user does while a script is busy (input, selection, the scroll bars, keys, then animations of transform and opacity, scroll boxes and the caret, drawn by chrome frames from the last layout). Hover stays the page's, by design (round 24, item 4).

After round 25. The list is in the order of its measures again: item 10 is item 2, done for two of what it named (legacy-html.html's task, identified and gone; p10k's first passes in part), and the profiler's bursts are in item 9. Item 1's figures were old: measured again they are higher, and nothing here says why.

After round 26. Heavy pages from the navigation to the load event: the first paint is halved on the mean (round 26), the load much less. What is left of it is item 1 below and two things of its own. The engine's share of the window thread during a load is 47 to 68 % on most of them (vimeo.com: the interpreter 27 %, the collection 13 %, the rest spread out). css-tricks.com is the engine too, 18 s for its twenty-three embeds, now that they are all loaded. Not done: a preload scanner that works while the document arrives (the parser takes the whole document first: cnn.com's 6.8 MB, 240 to 700 ms before any request of the page); priority headers (RFC 9218) now that images go out beside scripts; a style pass scoped to what a sheet that arrives can reach (cnn.com: 15 full passes for sheets, 2.2 s).

After round 29. The JIT reaches what pages run (round 29): nothing refused, 72 to 89 % of the interpreter's checks in compiled code on the pages measured. The loads did not follow, and the CPU went up. In order: what holds a load on a quiet machine, measured on the window thread by phase and against the waterfall, before more work on the engine; what a translation costs: each guard's exit materializes the stack in Wasm code (47 bytes of module for one of bytecode), a table of stack maps read by jit_exit would make an exit a few bytes; the translation itself is on the window thread (9 % of theverge.com's samples before the undo record was made small); identical code compiled once per realm (css-tricks.com's embeds); locals typed from the recorded runs (a whole function holds them in memory as values); inline caches for the interpreter's get_field where code stays cold; frontend_compile, 10 to 19 % of the window thread's engine samples, scripts under javascript.compile.offthread_min_bytes; the collection (10 to 16 %), generations or a floor above GC_MIN_ALLOCATION.

After round 30. A heavy page's load is the window thread's, busy from the first script to the load event, in the engine (natives, property definition, allocation, the collection, not the interpreter's dispatch alone) and the layouts it forces. The JIT no longer works against the load, and does not help it either. In order: a call through one site with a few callees (npr.org: 41 % of its JavaScript is while (!o.step()), 250 ns a call); the collection (1 s of theverge.com's 7: generations, its share is not a question of memory, round 30); what getComputedStyle and a forced layout cost on cnn.com (2 s); the engine's natives by a direct measure each; a compiler for a load, cheap enough to pay in seconds (Winch was not tried: wasm.wasmtime.compiler is the engine's whole, the JavaScript engine's own code included). Round 29's first item is done: what follows that names lazy compilation or bytecode sharing is not first by the numbers.

After round 31. "A call through one site" was the wrong name for npr.org's first item: what cost was inside the callees, one instruction in eight of what real pages run leaving the interpreter's hot loop (round 31: this, element reads of names, bitwise operators on doubles, === of strings, closures, object literals). In order: cnn.com's full style passes (18 of 27 for "too much changed", 4 200 of 11 200 elements marked whole by half a dozen mutations on divs: which rule; a partial restyle of a third of the document is slower than a full pass, why); what the engine costs on a page, whatever the path: a call of a function is 900 of a method call's Wasm instructions (frame_push, hot_return), a callback from a native a nested interp_run (2 600 an element of forEach); new the same; a compiler for a load (a baseline, Winch not tried); then the collection (10 to 13 % of the engine: generations), a lazy prototype; getComputedStyle without layout is worth 5 to 10 ms a call, no more. Measure with jsengine cost first: wall time on this machine, these weeks, says little under 10 %.

After round 33. The first item of the list after round 31 is done for what it named: cnn.com's marks were unions of reaches, not a rule; 28 full passes are 8, the load -16 %, its CPU -36 % (round 33). A forced read's cost is the style pass, not layout. What leads now, on all four pages, is the engine: the list after round 31 from its second item on. Of style: what restyle_needed is asked for, mid-sheet insertRule, mark_keyed. After round 34. Reading the machine code paid more than any profile so far. In order: the epoch check (12 to 20 % of all the engine's code: an engine of its own for the JavaScript image, polls in the natives); what a first paint waits for in a frame (bbc.com/news: three timers of 300 to 430 ms before it); compile on arrival by default (DOMContentLoaded -18 to -32 % on two pages, 3 runs); verification at the first closure; set_property of a new key without the walk of the prototypes; then the callback from a native, the collection. -o:speed is the engine's level now: what is said above of -o:size is history. After round 36. The epoch check is gone from the engine (round 36), new no longer walks the prototypes for a new key. The interpreter is 12 to 34 % faster by micro.js; two of the four loads followed. In order: the engine's time on the window thread for a load, measured as such (wasm.guest_time in api.stats): CPU to the load event no longer says it, cnn.com and bbc.com/news spend more of it than before for reasons not established; then what a first paint waits for in a frame, compile on arrival by default, verification at the first closure, ip at dispatch, the callback from a native, the collection. After round 40. A forced read's and a frame's pass on cnn.com: partial passes restyled what no change reached, through :has() above all (round 40): load -19 %. In order, of style: what :has() that is not exact costs a restyle, the full passes that remain (@keyframes in use, sheets that style another tree), resh_hits for each sheet that arrives. A read answered from less than the whole layout is worth a tenth of a read. After round 49: a load is the sum of what the window thread runs up to it: a sleep after each task moves the load by as much, from the first percent, and without collections theverge.com loads 301 ms sooner, ranges apart; the chains of scripts wait in that queue and no reordering gives time back. What a restyle marked for nothing is gone where it was a place read wrongly (:first-child and the like, a :has() in a :not(), :has(+ x) tried on every sibling): cnn.com -18 %, ranges apart. In order: the speed of scripts, then collections (265 ms of theverge.com, the ceiling of generations), then what custom properties written on the root force on cnn.com. After round 48: the window thread is 85 to 95 % busy up to the load event and the network is not on the path; what held cnn.com was that thread standing still for a compile (load -18 %). A body read sooner or compiled from the network takes nothing off a load: a script ready sooner waits for its turn. In order: what an element restyled costs (50 to 90 us, nine in ten for no change on cnn.com), then the tasks that stand between two steps of a page's chain of scripts. After round 47: frames on threads, inline caches, kept JIT profiles and generations were measured and take nothing off a load; see that round. After round 46. What a load runs is flat and interpreted: the two items that paid were algorithms (a regexp quadratic on a token, a walk of the document for each name nothing has), found by reading a sampler that does not wait for a poll. In order, of the engine: what scripts force of style and layout (43 % of cnn.com's Guest), get_field's misses, the free lists' cold blocks, new URL, the timeline in JSON at each call; ip at dispatch and native callbacks showed nothing of their own.

  1. The script stage of DOM-heavy pages, what is left (js_nodes10k on a quiet machine after round 25, 5 runs: a frame of 16.9 ms (16.8 to 17.4), the Animation phase 10.5 ms, where this list kept 17.7 and 11.8; the 20.6 to 29.5 ms first noted for that day were the load of the agents working beside the measure, nothing to bisect). In order of the engine's samples: the interpreter itself (interp_hot 17 % before round 15's 15 to 25 % on the loop's own instructions, call_native and the bridge 8 %; a DOM call costs 50 to 100 ns over the loop); the collection the DOM asks for (2.9 ms every 2 frames: the browser's Node_unpinAll, the prologue's walk of every wrapper with JS_IsUntouched for each, the finalizers' chain of calls, the sweep's frees, gc_drain); the browser's insertions (0.5 ms a frame by the browser's sampler: the insertion hooks 29 %, the journal 23 %, check_insert 9 %); the browser's factories (create_element, pool_insert_tagged copying a Node by value, the pin, the interface); making the wrappers (6 %). Texts are still copied to the heap and freed one by one (create_text, about 0.1 ms a frame). Measured and left: a flag per interface for the unforgeable members of its chain (round 7); the finalizers' skipped calls, the pre-sweep walks in one, the prologue's walk inlined, temp_reset in place (round 12); the hot loop as a procedure of its own (round 15: 8 % slower than inlined).
  2. Pages loaded from the navigation (rounds 15 to 18 and 25; wrentool bench perf -Only p10k_nav,nav_..., p10k_renav for the samples), by cost: p10k's first contentful paint is 39.7 ms: its parser's thread about 16 (html.parse_into 10, then the sheet 4 to 5: the sheet waits for the whole document, on the same thread, when it could start with the </style>), then the window's thread 24: the layout about 11 (flat in the samples; place_element, the threads' paragraphs, growing lists: new_box still reallocates), the style pass 8 (the rebuild 3.3, the style threads 3.9). Then text.html's first paint (Paint_Items, DirectWrite's glyph_formats under platform_color_glyph, the bands, the outlines; _extendhfsf2 was a misnamed sample, round 25) and its two modes; the first realm (5 ms from response to script, instantiation included: the instance made on the read-ahead thread would take a part). A task that arrives during the swap chain's wait (a fixed refresh screen's whole wait, at most a refresh) still waits for its end: the latency object cannot be woken by the loop.
  3. Layout of DOM-heavy pages: the steps' own code (nodes10k: the Layout phase 5.3 ms a frame on the day of round 25, 3.1 ms when this was written; the page thread's full pass then: tree 0.96, layout 1.07, finish 0.32, display 0.37, bands 0.13 ms). Round 10 found the records' layout no gain, round 11 took the image search, the cut of the flow and the display item's padding. What the profile shows now, by cost: building the box tree (19 % of the page thread; place_element, and the layout threads' summaries of the styles); the block layout of the columns (34 %, no part above 0.11 ms in process: apply_shifts moving every box to its column, then the 2 500 items' own layout at about 150 ns each: a shorter path for an item whose paragraph came from the threads and whose style is its siblings' is what is left to try); finishing (finish itself 6 %); note_refresh_inputs (4.5 %: every display item and inline item read again after the list is made, which the shares making the list could note as they go); the bands (4.4 %).
  4. What a full style pass still costs per page (mutation_fullstyle, 3.34 ms of CPU a frame in all, 5 runs, round 25; the style stage 0.75 ms in the browser, a pass 0.57 ms in process with seven threads since round 14, four fifths of that on the threads since round 9): on the style threads, matching (match_chain, the families of pages whose elements are each of their own kind: modern-css, p10k, matched in full as before) and the journal's comparison of the pairs that differ; on the window thread, the weights of the subtrees (0.07 ms, one walk since round 9: weights the DOM keeps would cost every insertion).
  5. The temporary arenas of the window thread and of the thread pool (src/host): emptied by zeroing what they held after each frame or job (mem_free_all and its memset are 6 to 12 % of some pool threads' samples on nodes10k), and given back past their first block. Allocations that need no zero (make of what is overwritten whole) are the gain there, not when the zeroing happens (round 5, item 5).
  6. The atlas lock and the word cache's 64 locks (toolkit): toolkit 0.64.0 took the atlas lock once per run of glyphs and a word cache hit under a shared lock (its docs/locks.md: 8 threads, a word's shape 442 -> 194 ns, a glyph's bitmap 120 -> 17 ns); what is left is measuring the page's text again before any per-thread front.
  7. The style index's string tables (style/engine.odin:68-69): atoms (interned ids) and flat arrays by atom (looked up now only for the first element of each kind of a family).
  8. The job queues of the blocking pool, the image decoders, the script compiler and the caches (the table above): measured first (round 3: a lock-free queue lost to the loop's mutex); a worker's ordered_remove(0) is a cost of its own.
  9. The profiler: the threads' bursts of a few ms (round 25: 0 running of 44 807 samples on p10k, not explained; ETW's context switches would say); correct the bias of samples taken in a system call.
  10. The interpreter, what is left after its loop (round 15): the full dispatch of interp_run for what the loop leaves (closures made, arguments, spreads, destructuring of iterables: the two cases of macro.js that did not gain are there), and native callbacks (sort, forEach: an interp_run activation each). A handler added to the loop must call nothing itself (interp_hot.odin's header says how).
